For higher inflation to be associated with a higher steady-state capital-labor ratio requires that qMPK=qm < 0 (that is, higher money balances reduce the marginal product of capital; money and capital are substitutes in production). This discussion actually has, by ignoring taxes, excluded what is probably the most important reason that superneutrality may fail in actual economies. Taxes generally are not indexed to inflation and are levied on nominal capital gains instead of real capital gains.
